questions.question: State the unit of bandwidth. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• State the unit of bandwidth.
  • Explanation-2 mark
  • The unit of bandwidth is bits per second (bps) for digital signals, which can be scaled to
  • higher units like megabits per second (Mbps) and gigabits per second (Gbps). For analog
  • signals, bandwidth is measured in Hertz (Hz), which represents the range of frequencies
  • a channel can transmit.

questions.question: Describe bit interval and bit rate. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe bit interval and bit rate.
  • Explanation-2 mark
  • Bit interval is the time it takes to transmit a single bit, while bit rate is the number of bits
  • transmitted per se cond. In other words, bit rate is the inverse of the bit interval, as it
  • measures how many of those time slots for a single bit fit into one second. Bit rate is
  • typically expressed in bits per second (bps), with common prefixes like kilobits per
  • second (Kbps) and megabits per second (Mbps).

questions.question: Differentiate between Stop-and-Wait ARQ and Go-Back-N ARQ with respect to any one key feature. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Differentiate between Stop -and-Wait ARQ and Go -Back-N ARQ with respect to
  • any one key feature.
  • Any two points-1 mark for each
  • Stop and Wait GoBackN
  • In the Stop and Wait protocol, the sender
  • sends one frame and then waits for the
  • receiver to acknowledge it.
  • Any frames that were sent after the frame
  • that is believed to have been damaged or
  • lost are resent.
  • In the Stop and Wait protocol, the
  • Sender window size is 1.
  • In the Go -Back-N protocol, the Sender
  • window size is N.
  • In the Stop and Wait protocol, the
  • receiver window size is 1.
  • In the Go -Back-N protocol, the receiver
  • window size is 1.
  • No particular sequence needs to be
  • followed at the receiver end of the Stop
  • and Wait protocol.
  • The Go-Back-N protocol's receiver end will
  • only accept the correct sequence.
  • In the Stop and Wait protocol, the
  • transmission type is Half duplex.
  • In the Go -Back-N protocol, the
  • transmission type is full duplex.
  • Efficiency formula for the Stop and Wait
  • protocol is 1/(1+2*a), where a is the ratio
  • of propagation delay to transmission
  • delay.
  • Efficiency formula for the Go -Back-N
  • protocol is N/(1+2*a), where a is the
  • proportion of propagation delay to
  • transmission delay and N is the number of
  • packets transmitted.

questions.question: Recall which protocol is considered the basis for Ethernet. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Recall which protocol is considered the basis for Ethernet.
  • Explanation-2 mark
  • Ethernet uses the IEEE 802.3 standard which defines protocols for the Physical and Data
  • Link layers of the OSI model. On the Data Link layer, it splits into the Logical Link Control
  • (LLC) and Media Access Control (MAC) layers, with the MAC layer using a me chanism
  • called CSMA/CD (Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection) to manage
  • how devices share the network.

questions.question: Name and briefly describe the function of at least three common application layer protocols / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Name and briefly descr ibe the function of at least three common application
  • layer protocols.
  • Explanation-5 mark
  • HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol): This is the foundation of data communication for
  • the World Wide Web. It is used by web browsers to request and receive web pages,
  • images, and other resources from web servers, allowing users to browse the internet.
  • SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol): This protocol is essential for email services and
  • is used to send and forward email messages from a client to a mail server, as well as
  • between different mail servers across the internet.
  • DNS (Domain Name System): The DNS provides the "internet's phonebook" service,
  • translating human-readable domain names (e.g., www.example.com) into numerical IP
  • addresses that computers use to locate and connect with each other.
  • FTP (File Transfer Protocol): This protocol is used for transferring files between a client
  • and a server over a network. It allows users to upload, download, and manage files on a
  • remote system, using a separate control connection and data connection.

questions.question: Differentiate between stop - and- wait protocol and sliding window protocol / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Differentiate between stop - and- wait protocol and sliding window protocol.
  • Any five points-1 mark for each
  • Stop-and-Wait Protocol Sliding Window Protocol
  • In Stop-and-Wait Protocol, sender
  • sends one frame and wait for
  • acknowledgment from receiver side.
  • In sliding window protocol, sender
  • sends more than one frame to the
  • receiver side and re-transmits the
  • frame(s) which is/are damaged or
  • suspected.
  • Efficiency of Stop-and-Wait Protocol
  • is not that much good.
  • Efficiency of sliding window protocol is
  • better than stop and wait protocol.
  • Sender window size of Stop-and-
  • Wait Protocol is 1.
  • Sender window size of sliding window
  • protocol is N.
  • Receiver window size of Stop-and-
  • Wait Protocol is 1.
  • Receiver window size of sliding window
  • protocol may be 1 or N.
  • In Stop-and-Wait Protocol, sorting is
  • not necessary.
  • In sliding window protocol, sorting may
  • be or may not be necessary.
  • Efficiency of Stop-and-Wait Protocol
  • is 1/(1+2*a)
  • Efficiency of sliding window protocol is
  • N/(1+2*a)
  • Stop-and-Wait Protocol is half
  • duplex. Sliding window protocol is full duplex.
  • Stop-and-Wait Protocol Sliding Window Protocol
  • Stop-and-Wait Protocol is mostly
  • used in low speed and error free
  • network.
  • Sliding window protocol is mostly used
  • in high speed and error-prone network.
  • In Stop-and-Wait Protocol, the
  • sender cannot send any new frames
  • until it receives an acknowledgment
  • for the previous frame.
  • In sliding window protocol, the sender
  • can continue to send new frames even
  • if some of the earlier frames have not
  • yet been acknowledged.
  • Stop-and-Wait Protocol has a lower
  • throughput as it has a lot of idle time
  • while waiting for the
  • acknowledgment.
  • Sliding window protocol has a higher
  • throughput as it allows for continuous
  • transmission of frames.

questions.question: Explain how a firewall can prevent unauthorized access. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how a firewall can prevent unauthorized access.
  • Explanation-5 mark
  • A firewall prevents unauthorized access by acting as a barrier between networks,
  • inspecting incoming and outgoing data packets, and blocking any that don't meet
  • predefined security rules. It examines traffic based on criteria like IP addresses, ports,
  • and protocols, allowing only legitimate traffic to pass while blocking malicious or
  • suspicious activity to protect the network from threats like malware, hackers, and other
  • cyberattacks.

questions.question: Explain any two techniques used for congestion control. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain any two techniques used for congestion control.
  • Explanation-2.5 mark for each
  • Two techniques for congestion control are open -loop and closed-loop methods. Open-
  • loop techniques prevent congestion before it happens, often through rules like slow start
  • or leaky bucket algorithms to manage transmission rates. Closed -loop techniques, on
  • the other hand, are reactive and take action after congestion is detected, using feedback
  • mechanisms like choke packets or explicit congestion notification to signal a source to
  • slow down.

questions.question: Given a wireless system with limited bandwidth, how would you apply spread spectrum techniques to ensure that multiple users can access the network efficiently? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Given a wireless system with limited bandwidth, how would you apply spread
  • spectrum techniques to ensure t hat multiple users can access the network
  • efficiently?
  • Explanation with diagram-10 mark
  • To enable efficient multi-user access with spread spectrum in a limited bandwidth, Code
  • Division Multiple Access (CDMA) is used by assigning a unique spreading code to each
  • user, allowing them to share the same bandwidth simultaneously. The two main spread
  • spectrum techniques are Frequency Hopping (FHSS) , which rapidly changes the
  • frequency of the signal, and Direct Sequence (DSSS), which modulates the signal with
  • a pseudo-random code.
